CHIEF COMPLAINT
Recurrent kidney stones, hypertension and diabetes follow-up.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Angela is here today with concern for kidney stones. She reports pain has been up and down and she presented to the emergency room last week. She states the stone has since passed approximately three days ago. She denies current pain and denies blood in urine. She reports this is her 7th or 8th kidney stone episode. She was treated at the hospital with Percocet. She has not seen a urologist in about a year despite recurrent kidney stone episodes. Regarding her hypertension and diabetes, she continues on current management.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Denies chest pain. Denies abdominal pain. Reports previous issues with insomnia, currently somewhat improved with use of meditation apps. States she sometimes stays awake worrying about things. Has tried melatonin in the past without significant benefit. Denies other systemic symptoms.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Recurrent kidney stones (7th or 8th episode)
Hypertension
Type 2 diabetes mellitus (diagnosed 1 year ago)
Insomnia
Grade 2/6 systolic ejection murmur (known, unchanged)

MEDICATIONS
Norvasc 2.5 mg daily
Metformin 500 mg daily

ALLERGIES
Not documented.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not documented.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Works full-time. Reports limited time to prepare meals at home. Diet consists of frequent fast food, cakes, and cookies. Has difficulty eliminating fast food due to on-the-go lifestyle. Uses iPhone and meditation apps for sleep.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital Signs: Blood pressure 150/90 today. Home blood pressure readings 130-140/60-70 taken 2-3 times weekly. Previous readings around 180 systolic.
Lungs: Clear bilaterally, no crackles.
Heart: Grade 2/6 systolic ejection murmur, unchanged from prior exam.
Abdomen: Soft, no tenderness to palpation. Costovertebral angles nontender bilaterally.

RESULTS
A1C 6.7 (from last visit, improved from initial diagnosis one year ago).
Kidney stone appears to have passed.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Recurrent kidney stones: Patient appears to have passed current stone. Ordered urinalysis and urine culture to ensure resolution. Placed referral to urology (Dr. Harris) given recurrent episodes to evaluate for underlying etiology.

Hypertension: Currently well-controlled on Norvasc 2.5 mg daily with home blood pressures 130-140/60-70. Blood pressure today slightly elevated, likely white coat syndrome. No medication changes at this time. Continue current therapy with refills provided.

Type 2 diabetes: A1C 6.7, showing improvement. Continue Metformin 500 mg daily. Instructed patient to check blood sugars before each meal to better gauge food intake and carbohydrate management.

Nutrition: Placed referral to nutrition/dietitian counseling to address dietary sodium intake (goal <2300 mg/day) and overall diet modification, with goal of eventually reducing medication burden.

Insomnia: Counseled on sleep hygiene including turning off electronics, keeping room dark and cool, and using iPhone sleep mode. Patient prefers not to take prescription sleep medications. Prescribed melatonin 10 mg as needed. Encouraged continued use of meditation apps.

Follow-up: Return visit in 3 months.
